 Dated this the 4th day of October, 2024
 Judgment
The claimant in O.P.(M.V.) No.1389 of 2016 is the appellant herein.

He was aged 35 years at the
time of accident.

2. The short facts of the case reads as under:
On 14.1.2016 at 1.30 p.m., while the pe

titioner was working as a Conductor in a bus bearing registration No. KL-43-A-9783 driven by the 2nd respondent from east to west through Edakochi-Palluruthy road and when the bus reached near Janatha junction, the 2 nd respondent applied sudden brake in a negligent manner, as a result of which, the petitioner fell inside the bus and sustained severe injuries.

Since petitioner suffered head injury, EDH and fracture base of right middle finger, he was referred to the Government Medical College Hospital, Kottayam and 5% disability was assessed as per Ext.X1 disability certificate.
3. The insurance company entered appearance and contested the claim.
They filed a written statement contending that the insured MACA NO. 74 OF 2021 3 2024:KER:73944 neither reported the accident nor produced the vehicular documents for verification.

It was also contended that, as per the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act, the covered employees of the insured are eligible to get compensation only under the Employees Compensation Act and, the claim petition was not maintainable.
4. Before the tribunal Exts.A1 to A8 were marked on the side of the appellant and Ext.X1, the disability certificate, was marked as Court Exhibit.

The tribunal, based on the evidence on record,
framed the following issues:
" 1.
Whether the petitioner sustained injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of the 2nd respondent?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to get compensation from the respondents?
and if so, what is the quantum?

3. Reliefs and costs."

sentences.text: Though, the appellant claimed that he was drawing an income of Rs.18,000/- per month, no evidence has been produced, and hence, the tribunal fixed the notional income at Rs.10,000/-.

It is against the said finding and also the insufficiency of compensation under the non pecuniary heads that the appellant has approached this MACA NO. 74 OF 2021 4 2024:KER:73944 Court with this appeal.

6. Heard Sri. V.A. Omanakuttan, the learned counsel appearing for the appellant and Sri. Thomas Mathew Nellimootil, the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the insurance company.
7.

The learned counsel appearing for the appellant contended that, going by the provisions contained under The Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Payment of Fair Wages Act, 1971, a conductor is considered to be a semi skilled worker.

entities.text: Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Payment of Fair Wages Act, 1971
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: He further relied on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Manusha Sreekumar and Others vs. The United India Insurance Company Ltd. [AIR 2022 SC 5161] to contend that even for a driver Rs.15,600/- was fixed as the notional income and if the same parameters are adopted in this case, the income would be more than what was fixed by the tribunal.

entities.text: Manusha Sreekumar and Others vs. The United India Insurance Company Ltd. [AIR 2022 SC 5161]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned counsel also submitted that under the heads pain and sufferings and also loss of amenities, suitable enhancement may be granted.

8. On the other hand, the learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submitted that the conductor in a bus cannot be equated with a skilled worker like a driver and, therefore, the MACA NO. 74 OF 2021 5 2024:KER:73944 principles followed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Manusha Sreekumar (Supra) cannot be applied to the facts of the present case.
According to the learned Standing Counsel, just and fair compensation has already been awarded by the learned Tribunal.
9. I have considered the rival submissions raised across the Bar.
10. No doubt, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Manusha Sreekumar (Supra) had fixed the income of the driver at Rs.15,600/-.
However, the same may not strictly apply in a case of a conductor.

However, it is to be noted that while fixing the notional income in the case of a conductor who is admittedly a semi skilled worker going by the provisions contained under The Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Payment of Fair Wages Act, 1971, the same ought to be that of a coolie worker.

entities.text: Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Payment of Fair Wages Act, 1971
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 11. In the peculiar facts and circumstances, this Court feels it appropriate to fix the notional income of the claimant at Rs.12,000/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to get an amount of Rs.60,000/- (12000x5) under the head Loss of earnings.
The tribunal has already awarded an amount of Rs.30,000/- on that head.
Hence, MACA NO. 74 OF 2021 6 2024:KER:73944 the appellant is entitled to get an amount of Rs.30,000/- as enhanced compensation.

As the notional income is taken as Rs.12,000/-, the appellant is entitled to get an amount of Rs.1,15,200/-
(12,000x12x16x5/100) under the head compensation for continuing permanent disability.

The tribunal had already awarded an amount of Rs.96,000/- and accordingly, the appellant is entitled to get Rs.19,200/- as additional compensation under the head compensation for continuing permanent disability.

Similarly an additional amount of Rs.15,000/- is awarded towards Compensation for pain and sufferings, and an additional amount of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards Compensation for loss of amenities and comforts.

Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to get an Akhil vs United India Insurance Company Limited on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52043781/
3 additional amount of Rs.74,200/- (Rupees Seventy Four Thousand Two Hundred only) as enhanced compensation as follows:
 Heads

Enhanced amount  Loss of earnings 30,000/-
 Compensation for pain and sufferings 15,000/-
Compensation for loss of amenities and10,000/-
 MACA NO. 74 OF 2021 7 2024:KER:73944  comforts Compensation for continuing permanent 19,200/- disability Total enhanced compensation 74,200/-
The aforesaid amount will carry interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of petition till realization with proportionate cost.
The appellant shall furnish the details of the bank account to the insurance company for transfer of the amount.
The insurance company shall deposit the amount within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
It is made clear that the appellant is not entitled to get interest for 253 days caused for the delay in filing the application.
Appeal ordered accordingly.
